capabilities: Render nested objects and arrays as a collapsible tree in the Properties panel
Edit, add, remove and reorder nested entries in place and change a nested property's type
Type one-line YAML collections that convert into objects, lists, or lists of objects
Rename or delete a nested key across the whole vault, with git commits and undo for bulk operations
Search nested properties and control the initial expand level per vault or per note
extras: Documentation is itself a demo vault (installable via a command, release zip, or the repository); beta versions install via BRAT; git-based commit and undo of bulk operations requires the vault to be in a git repository.
motivation: The README says the plugin was inspired by a community feature request for nested frontmatter support.
problem: Obsidian's Properties editor does not display nested frontmatter, so users must read and change nested values by editing raw YAML by hand.

relations.evidence: Narrower focus: nesting; vault-wide rename/delete and search
Broader nesting UI: collapsible tree, type changes, vault-wide rename/delete and search
Broader nesting scope: arbitrary nested objects and arrays
Alternative UI: edits nested values through Properties rows
Alternative UI: keeps Properties and gives each nested key a row

summary: Adds nested YAML frontmatter support to the Properties panel, rendering objects and arrays as an editable collapsible tree.
